newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's Kim puts priority on improving economy.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's Kim puts priority on improving economy.

text.p: South Korean President Kim Young-sam said on Tuesday the priority for the government this year would be improving economic competitiveness.
"The first priority of the government policies for this year will be placed on enhancing the competitiveness of the nation's economy," Kim told a news conference.
He said the economy was facing difficulties because of a substantially increased current account deficit.

"This is largely due to lower prices for semiconductors and steel products that are among our major export items. Basically however, it is because the attitude of those involved in economic activity and our institutions and practices remain largely unchanged," he said.

Kim said by ignoring the need to restructure, the Korean economy has perpetuated a high-cost, low-efficiency system that has weakened competitiveness at a time of intensified international competition.

"During this year, we must first of all improve the business environment in a major way to encourage firms to increase their investments and also to make our country very attractive to foreign investors all over the world," he said.
Kim also said he would establish a committee on financial reform in the near future that would be placed directly under his direction to reform the financial sector.
He said the government would strongly push economic policy aimed at lowering interest rates, land prices and the cost of distribution, helping businesses strengthen competitiveness.

Kim said the nation should try to drastically reduce the balance of international payment deficits this year by cutting down on unessential and unnecessary foreign exchange spending and conserve energy.

"To discourage wasteful consumption, the administration will improve relevant systems and spearhead a move to eliminate wasteful spending and inefficiency in the public sector. By doing so, the government will try to save more than one trillion won," he said.
